title: Dr. Bob Cheng 鄭寶鼎博士
content_html:
Dr. Bob Cheng (鄭寶鼎博士) was a Taiwanese American chemist, entrepreneur, philanthropist, and community leader, and the founder of the Taiwanese American History (T.A.H.) Archives Center in Irvine, California. He was born in Taiwan, where he earned his undergraduate degree from National Taiwan University, before emigrating to the United States to earn his Ph.D. in Chemistry from Syracuse University in 1969. He founded and built a successful electronics company, which provided the resources he would later devote to the Taiwanese American community.

Bob was a quiet and consistent presence in Taiwanese American civic life for decades before founding the Archives. In the 1990s and early 2000s, he organized annual Taiwanese American softball tournaments in central New Jersey that drew teams from across the East Coast, becoming a beloved gathering point for the second generation. He founded the Windsor Area Taiwanese American Association (WATAA) in central New Jersey and established one of the largest Taiwanese American scholarship programs in the country, anonymously funding community scholarships for high school seniors across more than a dozen cities nationwide for over a decade.

His defining legacy is the T.A.H. Archives Center. Alarmed that the first generation of Taiwanese Americans, those who had arrived in the 1950s and 60s to pursue graduate education and a better life, was aging and that their stories risked being lost, Bob convened the first planning meeting in 2010 with a small group of community leaders in Orange County. In 2014, he personally funded the lease of a 4,000-square-foot facility in Irvine. In 2016, he purchased outright a 19,000-square-foot standalone building in Irvine’s Corporate Park, envisioning it as a museum-quality cultural center for the Taiwanese American community. He tirelessly solicited donations of books, photographs, newsletters, artifacts, and organizational records from Taiwanese American communities across the country, and made the space freely available to community groups on weekends.

Bob passed away on September 20, 2020. Those who knew him consistently described him as modest, determined, and deeply generous, a man who gave anonymously, worked without seeking recognition, and held a vision he pursued with quiet persistence over decades. As one eulogist wrote, he “lit the flame for all of us to remember our struggles and our successes as Taiwanese Americans.”

Dr. Bob Cheng (鄭寶鼎博士) was a Taiwanese American chemist, entrepreneur, philanthropist, and community leader, and the founder of the Taiwanese American History (T.A.H.) Archives Center in Irvine, California. He was born in Taiwan, where he earned his undergraduate degree from National Taiwan University, before emigrating to the United States to earn his Ph.D. in Chemistry from Syracuse University in 1969. He founded and built a successful electronics company, which provided the resources he would later devote to the Taiwanese American community.

Bob was a quiet and consistent presence in Taiwanese American civic life for decades before founding the Archives. In the 1990s and early 2000s, he organized annual Taiwanese American softball tournaments in central New Jersey that drew teams from across the East Coast, becoming a beloved gathering point for the second generation. He founded the Windsor Area Taiwanese American Association (WATAA) in central New Jersey and established one of the largest Taiwanese American scholarship programs in the country, anonymously funding community scholarships for high school seniors across more than a dozen cities nationwide for over a decade.

His defining legacy is the T.A.H. Archives Center. Alarmed that the first generation of Taiwanese Americans, those who had arrived in the 1950s and 60s to pursue graduate education and a better life, was aging and that their stories risked being lost, Bob convened the first planning meeting in 2010 with a small group of community leaders in Orange County. In 2014, he personally funded the lease of a 4,000-square-foot facility in Irvine. In 2016, he purchased outright a 19,000-square-foot standalone building in Irvine’s Corporate Park, envisioning it as a museum-quality cultural center for the Taiwanese American community. He tirelessly solicited donations of books, photographs, newsletters, artifacts, and organizational records from Taiwanese American communities across the country, and made the space freely available to community groups on weekends.

Bob passed away on September 20, 2020. Those who knew him consistently described him as modest, determined, and deeply generous, a man who gave anonymously, worked without seeking recognition, and held a vision he pursued with quiet persistence over decades. As one eulogist wrote, he “lit the flame for all of us to remember our struggles and our successes as Taiwanese Americans.”
